Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Tennis Shock Basel loss dents Djokovic’s ATP Finals hopes Source : BBC 1 November 2026 10:22pm Novak Djokovic is playing in Basel for the first time since 2011 Audio By Carbonatix
Novak Djokovic's hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.
Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5), the first time Struff has beaten him in nine meetings.
"I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy," said the world number 27.
"I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. He beat me very, very easily the last eight times. So, I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance."
The year's top-eight performers qualify for the ATP event in Turin and this result leaves Djokovic - the men's game's record 24-time Grand Slam winner - 11th in the standings.
Djokovic admitted he expected to feel "a little rusty" after beating Frenchman Ugo Humbert on Wednesday, but now faces a fight to reach the final as he is outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018.
Rafael Jodar holds the final qualifying spot in ninth place, because number one Jannik Sinner is injured and will not take part.
Djokovic is 319 points behind Jodar, but he can move up the rankings at the Paris Masters in November.
The Serb aims to overtake Roger Federer with his 19th appearance in the Turin final.
He has won the event a record seven times and missed the past two editions with injury, but the last time he failed to qualify on merit was in 2017, when injury affected his season.
Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have their places confirmed for the showpiece event in Italy from 15-22 November, although American Shelton also surprisingly lost in Basel.
The top seed lost 6-3 6-7 (4-7) 7-6 (7-1) to Swiss wildcard Jerome Kym, who is ranked 222nd in the world.
